A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same underlying causal fairness framework and retain corresponding methods, datasets and experiments despite substantial renaming and reframing. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original medical-image classification experiments on MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert and TCGA-LUAD, together with transfer evaluations, ablations and GradCAM analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original medical-image experiments and adds baseline comparisons, demographic evaluations, synthetic causal-effect validation and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The central JSD-MI pretraining, additive masking, conditioned discriminator, losses and alternating optimization remain unchanged. Appendix D.4 adds limited proposed adaptations: matching the discriminator head to multivalued sensitive attributes and conditioning on fair-path parents for richer causal graphs.

E1.justification: The three medical datasets, diagnosis tasks and eight downstream MIMIC-CXR tasks are retained. V2 adds focused coverage through a synthetic SCM, age-based fairness evaluation across the three datasets, and joint gender-by-age evaluation on MIMIC-CXR (Table 3; Appendices D.2 and D.4).

E2.justification: V2 adds SUBG and Group-DRO to the main comparison on all three datasets, retaining Vanilla, AD and FAAP. This substantially broadens the central comparison to include data balancing and worst-group robust training alongside the original adversarial approaches.

E3.justification: The main 90/10 split and stated hyperparameters are retained. Supplementary protocols add an 80/10/10 train/validation/test split with validation-based tuning, an age threshold of 60, and synthetic interventional DE/IE evaluation. Renaming EO to EOp and ADF to EOd preserves their formulas and does not change the retained metrics.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of direct-effect suppression versus indirect-effect preservation, validation-based hyperparameter selection, age and joint-attribute robustness, demographic composition, and computational overhead. These substantially extend the retained architecture and hyperparameter ablations, downstream transfer evaluation and GradCAM analysis.

E5.justification: V1 presents point estimates without run counts or uncertainty. V2 introduces mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting throughout Table 1, discloses five repetitions in Appendix C.1, and reports five-seed averaging for the synthetic experiment. This establishes a substantial reporting change without establishing whether the retained experiments were rerun.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for new baselines, demographic settings and appendix studies, including synthetic SPARC direct and indirect effects of 0.027 and 0.171. Shared Table 1 point estimates remain unchanged, but ablation values change: Table 2 MIMIC ResNet50 accuracy changes from 84.67% to 84.26%, and the CheXpert CMI values at noise strengths 0.2 and 0.3 are interchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A substantially rewrites Theorem 1's proof, restoring summation over X and explicitly invoking ignorability and consistency. V2 removes v1's reversed sufficiency statement following Theorem 2 and introduces an epsilon-relaxed PSCF definition. These are mathematical revisions beyond relocating proofs or changing notation.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds a novel Diagnosis Fairness criterion and Approximate Diagnosis Fairness metric for medical diagnosis. V2 replaces that novelty claim with scalable enforcement of existing path-specific counterfactual fairness through conditional independence and a connection to standard equalized odds, broadening the claimed scope to high-dimensional modalities.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of baseline over-correction and under-correction, acknowledges omitted exogenous influences, and explains that its sufficient independence constraint can suppress information that PSCF would permit. These materially qualify the causal mechanism and applicability, alongside new interpretations of synthetic and demographic experiments.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a repository address and reports code availability, whereas v1 only promises release; Appendix C.3 still retains the future-release wording. It also adds component FLOP costs, synthetic-generation parameters and statements about shared training and tuning controls. Existing hardware, software and principal hyperparameter disclosures are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands causal-fairness positioning, including Kusner's counterfactual fairness, Chiappa and Gillam's PSCF, and information-theoretic equalized-odds literature. It replaces v1's assertion that prior fairness metrics are causal-model agnostic with a contribution explicitly framed around making established PSCF tractable.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution statements and conclusion are extensively rewritten around SPARC. Theory now precedes the method instantiation, proofs move to Appendix A, and the appendices are reorganized into theory, settings, implementation and additional experiments. This exceeds terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document from two columns to one, redraws the causal diagram, expands Table 1 with uncertainty and ranking annotations, and adds demographic plots and supplementary tables. Figures 2–4 retain their underlying content while being resized or relocated; the overall visual organization changes substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves the paper's theoretical grounding and empirical support: it repairs v1's reversed implication and proof derivation, acknowledges existing PSCF/equalized-odds concepts, and adds direct causal-effect validation, broader baselines and repeated-run uncertainty. These address important weaknesses in the original justification. Table 9's caption and protocol description remain inconsistent, and output fairness still cannot certify the stronger input-independence condition, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains.
